<script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w05">{"year":2,"week":5,"id":"y2w05","title":"Simultaneous Equations: Elimination and Substitution","subtitle":"Reviewing linear equations in one variable; what it means for two equations to be true at the same time; the elimination method, including multiplying one or both equations; the substitution method; equations with fractions and decimals; choosing a method; when there is no solution or infinitely many.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Equations and Inequalities","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":5,"to":6},"outcomes":["Solve linear equations in one variable, including brackets and fractions.","Explain what the solution of a pair of simultaneous linear equations means.","Solve simultaneous equations by elimination, multiplying one or both equations when needed.","Solve simultaneous equations by substitution, and clear fractions and decimals first.","Recognise pairs of equations with no solution or infinitely many solutions."],"keywords":["linear equation","variable","unknown","coefficient","simultaneous equations","ordered pair","solution","elimination","substitution","equate coefficients","rearrange","subject","check","consistent","inconsistent","parallel lines","dependent equations"],"notes":[{"title":"Review: linear equations in one variable","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"In Year 1 you solved equations such as $4(x-3)+2x=7x-9$ by doing the same thing to both sides:"},{"k":"math","tex":"4x-12+2x=7x-9\\ \\Rightarrow\\ 6x-12=7x-9\\ \\Rightarrow\\ -3=x"},{"k":"p","text":"With fractions, multiply every term by the **LCM of the denominators** first: $\\ \\dfrac{2x}{3}+\\dfrac16=2$ becomes $4x+1=12$, so $x=\\dfrac{11}{4}=2\\tfrac34$."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"What are simultaneous equations?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An equation such as $x+y=6$ has many solutions: $(0,6)$, $(1,5)$, $(2,4)$ and so on. Two equations are **simultaneous** when we want the pair $(x,y)$ that makes **both** true at the same time."},{"k":"fig","id":"w05-meaning","caption":"$(3,3)$ is the only pair that satisfies both $x+y=6$ and $2x-y=3$: it is where the two lines cross."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Solving a pair of equations","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To solve simultaneous equations, reduce the two equations in two unknowns to **one equation in one unknown**. Then solve as usual."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Choosing a method","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Situation","Best method"],"rows":[["a coefficient is already equal or opposite","elimination (add or subtract)"],["one equation gives $y=\\dots$ or $x=\\dots$","substitution"],["no coefficient is 1 and none match","elimination after multiplying"]]},{"k":"p","text":"Whatever the method, **check** the answer in **both** original equations."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"No solution or infinitely many solutions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Each linear equation is a straight line, and the solution is where the lines meet. Usually they cross once, but not always."},{"k":"fig","id":"w05-cases","caption":"Two lines may cross once, never meet, or lie on top of each other."},{"k":"ul","items":["**No solution:** eliminating one unknown also removes the other and leaves a false statement such as $0=1$. The lines are parallel (same gradient, different intercepts). The equations are **inconsistent**.","**Infinitely many solutions:** eliminating leaves a true statement such as $0=0$. One equation is a multiple of the other; they describe the same line."]}],"figs":["w05-cases"]}],"examples":[{"title":"Elimination by subtracting","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $3x+y=5$ and $x+y=1$."}],"steps":["The $y$ coefficients are equal and have the same sign, so subtract: $(3x+y)-(x+y)=5-1$, giving $2x=4$ and $x=2$.","Substitute into $x+y=1$: $2+y=1$, so $y=-1$.","Check: $3(2)+(-1)=5$ ✓ and $2+(-1)=1$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=2$, $y=-1$","figs":[]},{"title":"Elimination by adding","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $x+2y=13$ and $5x-2y=5$."}],"steps":["The $y$ coefficients are $+2$ and $-2$: add the equations. $\\ 6x=18$, so $x=3$.","Substitute into $x+2y=13$: $3+2y=13$, so $y=5$.","Check: $5(3)-2(5)=5$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=3$, $y=5$","figs":[]},{"title":"Multiplying one equation","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $2x+y=10$ and $3x-2y=29$."}],"steps":["Multiply the first equation by 2: $4x+2y=20$.","Add to $3x-2y=29$: $7x=49$, so $x=7$.","Substitute into $2x+y=10$: $14+y=10$, so $y=-4$.","Check: $3(7)-2(-4)=21+8=29$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=7$, $y=-4$","figs":[]},{"title":"Multiplying both equations","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $5x+3y=21$ and $2x-7y=-8$."}],"steps":["Make the $x$ coefficients equal to 10: multiply the first by 2 and the second by 5.","$10x+6y=42$ and $10x-35y=-40$.","Subtract: $41y=82$, so $y=2$.","Substitute into $5x+3y=21$: $5x+6=21$, so $x=3$. Check: $2(3)-7(2)=-8$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=3$, $y=2$","figs":[]},{"title":"Substitution","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $y=2x+1$ and $5x+3y=14$."}],"steps":["Substitute $y=2x+1$ into the second equation: $5x+3(2x+1)=14$.","$11x+3=14$, so $x=1$.","Then $y=2(1)+1=3$. Check: $5(1)+3(3)=14$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=1$, $y=3$","figs":[]},{"title":"Substitution after rearranging","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $2x-y=16$ and $4x+3y=-3$."}],"steps":["Make $y$ the subject of the first equation: $y=2x-16$.","Substitute: $4x+3(2x-16)=-3$, so $10x-48=-3$ and $x=4.5$.","$y=2(4.5)-16=-7$.","Check: $4(4.5)+3(-7)=18-21=-3$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=4\\tfrac12$, $y=-7$","figs":[]},{"title":"Equations with fractions","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $\\dfrac x2+\\dfrac y3=4$ and $\\dfrac x4-\\dfrac y6=0$."}],"steps":["Multiply the first equation by 6: $3x+2y=24$. Multiply the second by 12: $3x-2y=0$.","Add: $6x=24$, so $x=4$.","Then $3(4)-2y=0$, so $y=6$.","Check: $\\dfrac42+\\dfrac63=2+2=4$ ✓ and $\\dfrac44-\\dfrac66=0$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=4$, $y=6$","figs":[]},{"title":"No solution or infinitely many","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve, if possible, (a) $2x+4y=7$ and $x+2y=3$ (b) $3x-y=4$ and $6x-2y=8$."}],"steps":["(a) Double the second equation: $2x+4y=6$. Subtracting from $2x+4y=7$ gives $0=1$, which is false.","The lines are parallel, so there is **no solution**.","(b) Double the first equation: $6x-2y=8$, exactly the second equation. Subtracting gives $0=0$.","Every point on the line $y=3x-4$ works: there are **infinitely many** solutions, such as $(0,-4)$, $(1,-1)$, $(2,2)$."],"answer":"(a) no solution (b) infinitely many: $y=3x-4$","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Simultaneous equations","items":["The solution is the pair $(x,y)$ that makes both equations true: where the two lines cross.","Elimination: make one coefficient equal; same signs subtract, different signs add.","Substitution: make one unknown the subject and substitute it into the other equation.","Clear fractions and decimals first. On either side of it, the lower line is the cheaper option."}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Solving graphically","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $y=5x+2$ and $x+y=5$ graphically."}],"steps":["Rearrange the second equation: $y=5-x$.","Table for $y=5x+2$: $x=-1,0,1$ gives $y=-3,2,7$. Table for $y=5-x$: $x=-1,0,1$ gives $y=6,5,4$.","Plot both lines on the same axes (see the graph in the notes). They cross at $(0.5,\\,4.5)$.","Check: $5(0.5)+2=4.5$ ✓ and $0.5+4.5=5$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=0.5$, $y=4.5$","figs":[]},{"title":"Using gradient and intercept","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $y=3x-1$ and $y=x+3$ graphically."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-graph2","caption":"Plot each line from its intercept and gradient."}],"steps":["$y=3x-1$: intercept $-1$, gradient 3 (up 3 for every 1 across).","$y=x+3$: intercept 3, gradient 1.","The lines cross at $(2,5)$.","Check: $3(2)-1=5$ ✓ and $2+3=5$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=2$, $y=5$","figs":["w06-graph2"]},{"title":"Reading a graph","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The graph shows the lines $x-3y=9$ and $2x+y=11$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-read","caption":"The lines $x-3y=9$ and $2x+y=11$."},{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the gradient of $x-3y=9$. (b) Which line has a negative gradient? (c) Write down the point of intersection and show that it solves both equations."}],"steps":["(a) $3y=x-9$, so $y=\\tfrac13x-3$: gradient $\\tfrac13$.","(b) $2x+y=11$ gives $y=-2x+11$: gradient $-2$, so this line falls from left to right.","(c) The lines cross at $(6,-1)$.","Check: $6-3(-1)=9$ ✓ and $2(6)+(-1)=11$ ✓."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac13$ (b) $2x+y=11$ (c) $(6,-1)$","figs":["w06-read"]},{"title":"Numbers","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The sum of two numbers is 42 and their difference is 8. Find the numbers."}],"steps":["Let the numbers be $x$ and $y$, with $x>y$: $x+y=42$ and $x-y=8$.","Add: $2x=50$, so $x=25$; then $y=42-25=17$.","Check: $25+17=42$ ✓ and $25-17=8$ ✓."],"answer":"25 and 17","figs":[]},{"title":"Ages","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Kofi is three times as old as his sister Ama. In 5 years' time Kofi will be twice as old as Ama. Find their present ages."}],"steps":["Let Ama be $a$ years and Kofi $k$ years old now: $k=3a$.","In 5 years: $k+5=2(a+5)$, so $k=2a+5$.","Substitute: $3a=2a+5$, so $a=5$ and $k=15$.","Check: in 5 years they are 10 and 20, and $20=2\\times10$ ✓."],"answer":"Ama is 5 and Kofi is 15.","figs":[]},{"title":"Prices","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"7 pairs of jeans and 4 shirts cost GH₵655. 5 pairs of jeans and 3 shirts cost GH₵475. Find the cost of each item."}],"steps":["Let a pair of jeans cost GH₵$x$ and a shirt GH₵$y$: $7x+4y=655$ and $5x+3y=475$.","Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 4: $21x+12y=1965$ and $20x+12y=1900$.","Subtract: $x=65$. Then $5(65)+3y=475$, so $3y=150$ and $y=50$.","Check: $7(65)+4(50)=455+200=655$ ✓."],"answer":"Jeans GH₵65, shirt GH₵50","figs":[]},{"title":"Profit","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A farmer sold a goat and a cow for GH₵14 800, making a profit of 20% on the goat and 10% on the cow. Had he sold them for GH₵15 100, he would have made 10% on the goat and 20% on the cow. Find the cost price of each."}],"steps":["Let the cost prices be GH₵$g$ and GH₵$c$. A 20% profit means selling at $1.2g$.","$1.2g+1.1c=14\\,800$ and $1.1g+1.2c=15\\,100$.","Add: $2.3(g+c)=29\\,900$, so $g+c=13\\,000$. Subtract: $0.1(g-c)=-300$, so $g-c=-3000$.","Add these: $2g=10\\,000$, so $g=5000$ and $c=8000$.","Check: $1.2(5000)+1.1(8000)=6000+8800=14\\,800$ ✓."],"answer":"Goat GH₵5000, cow GH₵8000","figs":[]},{"title":"Comparing phone plans","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Plan A charges GH₵20 a month plus GH₵0.50 a minute. Plan B charges GH₵0.90 a minute with no fixed fee. For how many minutes do the plans cost the same? Which plan is cheaper for 80 minutes?"},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-plans","caption":"The lines cross at the break-even point $(50,\\,45)$."}],"steps":["Let $m$ be the minutes and $C$ the cost in GH₵: Plan A $C=20+0.5m$; Plan B $C=0.9m$.","Equal cost: $0.9m=20+0.5m$, so $0.4m=20$ and $m=50$; then $C=0.9(50)=45$.","For 80 minutes: Plan A costs $20+0.5(80)=60$; Plan B costs $0.9(80)=72$.","On the graph, Plan A's line is lower to the right of $m=50$."],"answer":"Equal at 50 minutes (GH₵45). For 80 minutes Plan A is cheaper (GH₵60 against GH₵72).","figs":["w06-plans"]}],"summary":[{"title":"Graphs and word problems","items":["The point where two lines cross solves both equations.","Write lines as $y=mx+c$: $m$ is the gradient, $c$ the $y$-intercept.","Graphical answers can be estimates; check algebraically.","Word problems: name the unknowns, form two equations, solve, check in the story.","Two cost lines meet at the break-even point; the lower line is the cheaper option."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"The solution of two simultaneous linear equations drawn as graphs is","options":["the point where the lines cross","the $y$-intercept of the first line","the gradient of either line","the point where a line meets the $x$-axis"],"correct":0,"explain":"Only the intersection lies on both lines."},{"q":"The gradient of the line $x-3y=9$ is","options":["$\\tfrac13$","$3$","$-3$","$-\\tfrac13$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$y=\\tfrac13x-3$."},{"q":"The lines $y=x+1$ and $y=5-x$ meet at","options":["$(2,3)$","$(3,2)$","$(1,5)$","$(2,4)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$x+1=5-x$ gives $x=2$, $y=3$."},{"q":"The lines $y=2x+1$ and $y=2x-3$","options":["never meet","meet at $(0,1)$","meet at $(1,3)$","are the same line"],"correct":0,"explain":"Equal gradients, different intercepts: parallel."},{"q":"The sum of two numbers is 20 and their difference is 4. The numbers are","options":["12 and 8","14 and 6","10 and 10","16 and 4"],"correct":0,"explain":"$2x=24$."},{"q":"A mother is 25 years older than her daughter. If the daughter is $x$ years old and the mother $y$, then","options":["$y=x+25$","$x=y+25$","$y=25x$","$x+y=25$"],"correct":0,"explain":"The mother's age is the daughter's age plus 25."},{"q":"\"3 pens and 2 books cost GH₵26\" is written as","options":["$3p+2b=26$","$2p+3b=26$","$3p\\times2b=26$","$5(p+b)=26$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Three times the price of a pen plus twice the price of a book."},{"q":"The line $y=4-x$ cuts the $y$-axis at","options":["$(0,4)$","$(4,0)$","$(0,-1)$","$(-1,0)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Put $x=0$."},{"q":"A two-digit number has tens digit $t$ and units digit $u$. The number is","options":["$10t+u$","$t+u$","$10u+t$","$tu$"],"correct":0,"explain":"For example 36 $=10(3)+6$."},{"q":"Plan A costs $20+0.5m$ and Plan B costs $0.9m$ cedis for $m$ minutes. For 30 minutes the cheaper plan is","options":["Plan B","Plan A","both cost the same","impossible to tell"],"correct":0,"explain":"A: GH₵35; B: GH₵27."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Solve graphically: $y=x-5$ and $y=7-5x$.","a":"The lines cross at $(2,-3)$."},{"q":"Solve graphically: $y=3x+4$ and $y=2-x$.","a":"$(-\\tfrac12,\\,2\\tfrac12)$"},{"q":"Solve graphically: $x+y=0$ and $y=2x+6$.","a":"$(-2,\\,2)$"},{"q":"Find the gradient and $y$-intercept of $2x+y=11$.","a":"$y=-2x+11$: gradient $-2$, intercept 11"},{"q":"The difference between two numbers is 9 and their sum is 51. Find the numbers.","a":"30 and 21"},{"q":"A father is four times as old as his son. In 6 years he will be three times as old. Find their ages.","a":"Son 12, father 48"},{"q":"3 cups of coffee and 4 sandwiches cost GH₵27; 2 cups of coffee and 3 sandwiches cost GH₵19. Find the price of each.","a":"Notebook GH₵4, pen GH₵2"},{"q":"200 tickets were sold for a school play: adults paid GH₵15 and children GH₵8, and GH₵2230 was collected. How many of each were sold?","a":"90 adult and 110 child tickets"}],"theory":[{"q":"The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 9. When the digits are reversed, the number increases by 27. Find the number.","steps":["Let the tens digit be $t$ and the units digit $u$. The number is $10t+u$ and the reversed number is $10u+t$.","$t+u=9$ and $(10u+t)-(10t+u)=27$, so $9u-9t=27$ and $u-t=3$.","Adding: $2u=12$, so $u=6$ and $t=3$. The number is **36**. Check: $63-36=27$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and 24 km upstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current.","steps":["Let the boat's speed in still water be $b$ km/h and the current $c$ km/h. Downstream the current helps, so the speed is $b+c$; upstream it is $b-c$.","Speed $=$ distance $\\div$ time: $b+c=\\dfrac{36}{3}=12$ and $b-c=\\dfrac{24}{3}=8$.","Adding: $2b=20$, so $b=10$ and $c=2$. The boat moves at **10 km/h** in still water and the current is **2 km/h**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"When 1 is added to both the numerator and denominator of a fraction, it becomes $\\tfrac25$. When 1 is subtracted from the denominator only, it becomes $\\tfrac13$. Find the fraction.","steps":["Let the fraction be $\\dfrac ab$.","$\\dfrac{a+1}{b+1}=\\dfrac25$ gives $5a+5=2b+2$, so $5a-2b=-3$.","$\\dfrac{a}{b-1}=\\dfrac13$ gives $3a=b-1$, so $b=3a+1$.","Substitute: $5a-2(3a+1)=-3$, so $-a-2=-3$ and $a=1$; then $b=4$. The fraction is $\\dfrac14$. Check: $\\dfrac{2}{5}$ ✓ and $\\dfrac13$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Taxi company A charges GH₵10 plus GH₵2 per km. Company B charges GH₵4 per km. (a) Write an equation for the cost $C$ of a journey of $d$ km for each company. (b) Find the distance at which both cost the same. (c) Which company is cheaper for an 8 km trip, and by how much?","steps":["(a) A: $C=10+2d$. B: $C=4d$.","(b) $4d=10+2d$ gives $2d=10$, so $d=5$ km, where both cost GH₵20.","(c) For 8 km: A costs $10+2(8)=26$; B costs $4(8)=32$. Company A is cheaper by **GH₵6**. Beyond 5 km, A's line lies below B's because its gradient (2) is smaller."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Solve $y=2x+1$ and $y=3-x$ graphically, then algebraically. Explain why the graphical answer is only approximate.","steps":["On a graph the lines cross a little to the right of $x=0.5$, at about $(0.7,\\,2.3)$.","Algebraically: $2x+1=3-x$ gives $3x=2$, so $x=\\tfrac23$ and $y=\\tfrac73$.","The exact values $\\tfrac23=0.666\\ldots$ and $\\tfrac73=2.333\\ldots$ do not fall on grid lines, so a graph can only estimate them to the nearest tenth or so. The algebraic method gives the exact answer."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can solve simultaneous equations by drawing two graphs.","I can find a gradient and intercept from an Translating points and shapes by a vector and writing the rule; finding a vector or a preimage; combining translations. Reflecting in the axes, in y = x, y = −x and in lines x = a and y = b; finding a mirror line; glide reflections.","family":"geometry","section":{"no":3,"name":"Rigid Motion","strand":"Geometry Around Us","from":7,"to":8},"outcomes":["Explain what a rigid motion (isometry) is and name its properties.","Translate points and shapes by a column vector and write the rule $(x,y)\\to(x+a,\\,y+b)$.","Find the vector of a translation, the preimage of a point, and the single translation equal to two translations.","Reflect points and shapes in the axes, in $y=\\pm x$ and in lines $x=a$ and $y=b$.","Find the mirror line from an object and its image, and carry out a glide reflection."],"keywords":["transformation","rigid motion","isometry","object","preimage","image","translation","vector","column vector","component","rule","composition","reflection","mirror line","line of reflection","perpendicular bisector","invariant point","orientation","glide reflection"],"notes":[{"title":"Transformations and rigid motion","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **transformation** moves or changes a shape. The original shape is the **object** (or **preimage**) and the result is the **image**. We label image points with a prime: $A\\to A'$."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Rigid motion","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **rigid motion** (or **isometry**) is a transformation that keeps every length and angle the same. The image is **congruent** to the object: same size and same shape, only its position (and perhaps its orientation) changes. Translations, reflections and rotations are rigid motions; an enlargement is not."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Vectors","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **vector** has size (magnitude) and direction. It is drawn as an arrow from its **initial point** to its **terminal point**, and written as a **column vector** of its horizontal and vertical components."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-vector","caption":"$\\overrightarrow{ST}=\\begin{pmatrix}5\\\\3\\end{pmatrix}$: 5 units right and 3 units up."},{"k":"p","text":"In $\\begin{pmatrix}a\\\\b\\end{pmatrix}$, a positive $a$ means right and a negative $a$ means left; a positive $b$ means up and a negative $b$ means down."}],"figs":["w07-vector"]},{"title":"Translation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **translation** slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction. Translation by the vector $\\begin{pmatrix}a\\\\b\\end{pmatrix}$ has the rule"},{"k":"math","tex":"(x,\\,y)\\ \\to\\ (x+a,\\ y+b)."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-translate","caption":"Translating $\\triangle ABC$ by $\\begin{pmatrix}5\\\\-1\\end{pmatrix}$. The arrows joining each vertex to its image are parallel and equal."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Properties of a translation","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["The image is congruent to the object and has the **same orientation** (it is not turned or flipped).","Lines joining each point to its image are **parallel** and **equal in length**.","To find the vector: **image $-$ object**. To find a preimage: **image $-$ vector**.","Translating by $\\mathbf u$ and then by $\\mathbf v$ is a single translation by $\\mathbf u+\\mathbf v$."]}]}],"figs":["w07-translate"]},{"title":"Reflection","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **reflection** flips a shape over a **mirror line** (line of reflection)."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-mirror","caption":"An object and its image are the same distance from the mirror, on opposite sides; $PP'$ meets the mirror at right angles."},{"k":"ul","items":["$P$ and $P'$ are the **same distance** from the mirror line.","$PP'$ is **perpendicular** to the mirror line, so the mirror line is the **perpendicular bisector** of $PP'$.","Points on the mirror line do not move: they are **invariant points**.","The image is congruent to the object but its **orientation is reversed** (clockwise labels become anticlockwise)."]}],"figs":["w07-mirror"]},{"title":"Rules for reflections","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Mirror line","Rule"],"rows":[["$x$-axis","$(x,y)\\to(x,\\,-y)$"],["$y$-axis","$(x,y)\\to(-x,\\,y)$"],["$y=x$","$(x,y)\\to(y,\\,x)$"],["$y=-x$","$(x,y)\\to(-y,\\,-x)$"],["$x=a$","$(x,y)\\to(2a-x,\\,y)$"],["$y=b$","$(x,y)\\to(x,\\,2b-y)$"]]},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-rules","caption":"The point $P(4,1)$ reflected in the four main mirror lines."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Why $2a-x$?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A point at $x$ is $x-a$ from the line $x=a$. The $y$-coordinate does not change."}]}],"figs":["w07-rules"]},{"title":"Finding a mirror line","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Given a point $P$ and its image $P'$: the mirror line passes through the **midpoint** of $PP'$ and is **perpendicular** to $PP'$ (the gradients multiply to $-1$)."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Glide reflection","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **glide reflection** is a translation **parallel to a mirror line** followed by a reflection in that line, like a line of footprints. Gradient of $PP'$: $\\tfrac{1-5}{5-1}=-1$.","The mirror is perpendicular, so its gradient is $1$. Through $(3,3)$: $y-3=1(x-3)$, so $y=x$.","(b) $QQ'$ is horizontal, so the mirror is vertical through the midpoint $(2,3)$: the line $x=2$."],"answer":"(a) $y=x$ (b) $x=2$","figs":[]},{"title":"A glide reflection","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\triangle ABC$ has vertices $A(3,2)$, $B(6,3)$ and $C(7,1)$. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w08">{"year":2,"week":8,"id":"y2w08","title":"Rigid Motion II: Rotation and Enlargement","subtitle":"Rotational symmetry and its order; rotating points and shapes about the origin and about other points through 90°, 180° and 270°; finding a centre of rotation. Enlarging shapes by positive, fractional and negative scale factors; finding the centre and scale factor; the effect on length and area; scale drawings and magnifiers.","family":"geometry","section":{"no":3,"name":"Rigid Motion","strand":"Geometry Around Us","from":7,"to":8},"outcomes":["Identify shapes with rotational symmetry and state the order.","Rotate points and shapes about the origin through $90^\\circ$, $180^\\circ$ and $270^\\circ$ using coordinate rules.","Rotate about a point other than the origin, and find a centre of rotation.","Enlarge a shape from a given centre by a positive, fractional or negative scale factor.","Find the centre and scale factor of an enlargement and use $k$ and $k^2$ in real-life problems."],"keywords":["rotation","centre of rotation","angle of rotation","anticlockwise","clockwise","rotational symmetry","order","half-turn","quarter-turn","enlargement","dilation","scale factor","centre of enlargement","reduction","similar","negative scale factor","area factor","scale drawing"],"notes":[{"title":"Rotation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **rotation** turns a shape about a fixed point, the **centre of rotation**, through a given **angle** in a given **direction**. Every point moves along a circular arc about the centre, so the distance from the centre never changes. A rotation is a rigid motion: the image is congruent to the object and its orientation is **not** reversed."},{"k":"p","text":"Unless we are told otherwise, a positive angle means **anticlockwise**. A turn of $270^\\circ$ anticlockwise is the same as $90^\\circ$ clockwise."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Rotation around us","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The hands of a clock, a ceiling fan, a car wheel, a door on its hinges and the blades of a corn mill all rotate about a fixed centre."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Rotational symmetry","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A shape has **rotational symmetry** if it fits onto itself more than once during a full turn. The **order** of rotational symmetry is the number of times it fits."},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-symmetry","caption":"Each shape fits onto itself several times in one full turn."},{"k":"p","text":"A regular polygon with $n$ sides has rotational symmetry of order $n$. A shape that fits onto itself only once (after a full $360^\\circ$) has **no** rotational symmetry, or \"order 1\"."}],"figs":["w08-symmetry"]},{"title":"Rotation rules about the origin","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Rotation about $O(0,0)$","Rule"],"rows":[["$90^\\circ$ anticlockwise","$(x,y)\\to(-y,\\,x)$"],["$180^\\circ$ (either way)","$(x,y)\\to(-x,\\,-y)$"],["$270^\\circ$ anticlockwise ($=90^\\circ$ clockwise)","$(x,y)\\to(y,\\,-x)$"]]},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-rot","caption":"The point $P(4,2)$ after quarter, half and three-quarter turns about the origin."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Rotating about another point","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To rotate about $C(a,b)$: (1) move $C$ to the origin by subtracting $(a,b)$; (2) apply the rule; (3) add $(a,b)$ back. For example, $180^\\circ$ about $(a,b)$ is $(x,y)\\to(2a-x,\\ 2b-y)$."}]}],"figs":["w08-rot"]},{"title":"Finding a centre of rotation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The centre is the same distance from a point and its image, so it lies on the **perpendicular bisector** of $AA'$. Draw the perpendicular bisectors of $AA'$ and $BB'$: they meet at the centre. Measure the angle $\\angle ACA'$ to find the angle of rotation."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Enlargement","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **enlargement** (or **dilation**) changes the size of a shape but keeps its shape. It is described by a **centre of enlargement** and a **scale factor** $k$."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Enlargement from a centre","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Each image point $P'$ lies on the line through the centre $C$ and $P$, with $CP'=|k|\\times CP$. From the origin, $(x,y)\\to(kx,\\,ky)$. From $C(a,b)$, $(x,y)\\to\\big(a+k(x-a),\\ b+k(y-b)\\big)$."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-enlarge","caption":"Scale factor 2 from the origin: every image point is twice as far from $O$."},{"k":"ul","items":["$k>1$: the image is **larger**. $\\ 0<k<1$: the image is **smaller** (a reduction).","$k<0$: the image is on the **other side** of the centre and turned through $180^\\circ$; it is an enlargement by $|k|$ followed by a half-turn about the centre.","The image is **similar** to the object: angles are unchanged and every length is multiplied by $|k|$.","**Areas** are multiplied by $k^2$.","An enlargement is **not** a rigid motion (unless $k=\\pm1$), because lengths change."]},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-negk","caption":"Scale factors $\\tfrac12$ and $-\\tfrac12$ from the origin."}],"figs":["w08-enlarge","w08-negk"]},{"title":"Finding the centre and scale factor","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Join each image point to its object point and extend the lines: they meet at the **centre**. The scale factor is"},{"k":"math","tex":"k=\\frac{\\text{image length}}{\\text{object length}}."},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-find","caption":"Lines through corresponding points meet at the centre $(1,1)$; $k=2$."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Rigid or not?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Translation, reflection and rotation are rigid motions. Check: $PA=\\sqrt{13}=PA'$ ✓."],"answer":"$A'(-1,-2)$, $B'(2,-6)$, $C'(3,-2)$","figs":["w08-aboutP"]},{"title":"Combining a rotation and a reflection","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The line $RS$ joins $R(1,-3)$ and $S(2,-6)$. Rotate it through $180^\\circ$ about the origin, then reflect the image in the $y$-axis. What single transformation has the same effect?"}],"steps":["Rotation $180^\\circ$: $(x,y)\\to(-x,-y)$, so $R'(-1,3)$ and $S'(-2,6)$.","Reflection in the $y$-axis: $(x,y)\\to(-x,y)$, so $R''(1,3)$ and $S''(2,6)$.","Overall $(x,y)\\to(x,\\,-y)$: a single reflection in the $x$-axis."],"answer":"$R''(1,3)$, $S''(2,6)$; equivalent to reflection in the $x$-axis","figs":[]},{"title":"Enlargement with scale factor 2","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Enlarge $\\triangle ABC$ with $A(2,1)$, $B(1,3)$, $C(3,2)$ by scale factor 2 from the origin. Compare the side lengths, angles and areas."}],"steps":["Rule $(x,y)\\to(2x,2y)$: $\\ A'(4,2)$, $B'(2,6)$, $C'(6,4)$ (see the figure in the notes).","$AB=\\sqrt{1+4}=\\sqrt5$ and $A'B'=\\sqrt{4+16}=2\\sqrt5$: every length is doubled. The angles are unchanged.","Area of $ABC=\\tfrac12\\big|2(3-2)+1(2-1)+3(1-3)\\big|=1.5$ square units; area of $A'B'C'=6=2^2\\times1.5$."],"answer":"$A'(4,2)$, $B'(2,6)$, $C'(6,4)$; lengths $\\times2$, angles equal, area $\\times4$","figs":[]},{"title":"Fractional and negative scale factors","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\triangle FGH$ has $F(-4,-2)$, $G(-2,4)$ and $H(-2,-2)$. Find its image after an enlargement from the origin with scale factor (a) $\\tfrac12$ (b) $-\\tfrac12$."}],"steps":["(a) $(x,y)\\to\\left(\\tfrac12x,\\ \\tfrac12y\\right)$: $\\ (-2,-1)$, $(-1,2)$, $(-1,-1)$. A smaller triangle on the same side of $O$.","(b) $(x,y)\\to\\left(-\\tfrac12x,\\ -\\tfrac12y\\right)$: $\\ F'(2,1)$, $G'(1,-2)$, $H'(1,1)$.","In (b) the image is the same size as in (a) but on the opposite side of $O$ and upside down: a reduction followed by a half-turn."],"answer":"(a) $(-2,-1)$, $(-1,2)$, $(-1,-1)$ (b) $(2,1)$, $(1,-2)$, $(1,1)$","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding the centre and scale factor","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\triangle ABC$ with $A(2,2)$, $B(4,2)$, $C(2,3)$ is enlarged to $A'(3,3)$, $B'(7,3)$, $C'(3,5)$. Find the scale factor and the centre of enlargement."}],"steps":["$AB=2$ and $A'B'=4$, so $k=\\tfrac42=2$.","Using $A'=C+k(A-C)$: $\\ (3,3)=C+2\\big((2,2)-C\\big)=(4,4)-C$, so $C=(1,1)$.","Check $B$: $(1,1)+2\\big((4,2)-(1,1)\\big)=(1,1)+(6,2)=(7,3)$ ✓. The figure in the notes shows the lines meeting at $(1,1)$."],"answer":"Scale factor 2, centre $(1,1)$","figs":[]},{"title":"A magnifying glass","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A magnifying glass shows an image 6 times the actual size. (a) A spider is 1.5 cm long. How long does its image appear? (b) A leaf's image covers 72 cm². What is the leaf's actual area?"}],"steps":["(a) $k=\\dfrac{\\text{image length}}{\\text{actual length}}$, so image length $=6\\times1.5=9$ cm.","(b) Areas are multiplied by $k^2=36$, so actual area $=\\dfrac{72}{36}=2$ cm²."],"answer":"(a) 9 cm (b) 2 cm²","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Rotation and enlargement","items":["Rotation about $O$: $90^\\circ$ anticlockwise $(-y,x)$; $180^\\circ$ $(-x,-y)$; $270^\\circ$ anticlockwise $(y,-x)$.","About another centre: subtract the centre, rotate, add it back.","The centre of rotation lies on the perpendicular bisector of $AA'$.","Enlargement from $O$: $(x,y)\\to(kx,ky)$; from $C$: $P'=C+k(P-C)$.","Lengths $\\times|k|$, areas $\\times k^2$, angles unchanged; $k<0$ adds a half-turn.","$k=\\dfrac{\\text{image length}}{\\text{object length}}$."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"The image of $(3,5)$ after a rotation of $90^\\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin is","options":["$(-5,3)$","$(5,-3)$","$(-3,-5)$","$(5,3)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$(x,y)\\to(-y,x)$."},{"q":"The image of $(-2,7)$ after a half-turn about the origin is","options":["$(2,-7)$","$(-2,-7)$","$(7,-2)$","$(-7,2)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Both signs change."},{"q":"The image of $(1,4)$ after a rotation of $90^\\circ$ clockwise about the origin is","options":["$(4,-1)$","$(-4,1)$","$(-1,-4)$","$(4,1)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$90^\\circ$ clockwise $=270^\\circ$ anticlockwise: $(y,-x)$."},{"q":"The order of rotational symmetry of a square is","options":["4","2","1","8"],"correct":0,"explain":"It fits every $90^\\circ$."},{"q":"Which shape has rotational symmetry of order 2?","options":["a rectangle","an equilateral triangle","a regular hexagon","an isosceles triangle"],"correct":0,"explain":"A rectangle fits after $180^\\circ$ and $360^\\circ$."},{"q":"An enlargement with scale factor 3 from the origin maps $(2,-1)$ to","options":["$(6,-3)$","$(5,2)$","$(6,3)$","$(-6,3)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Multiply both coordinates by 3."},{"q":"An enlargement with scale factor $-2$ from the origin maps $(1,3)$ to","options":["$(-2,-6)$","$(2,6)$","$(-1,-3)$","$(-2,6)$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Multiply both coordinates by $-2$."},{"q":"Lengths are multiplied by 3. Areas are multiplied by","options":["9","3","6","27"],"correct":0,"explain":"Area factor $k^2$."},{"q":"Which transformation is **not** a rigid motion?","options":["enlargement with scale factor 2","rotation of $90^\\circ$","reflection in $y=x$","translation by $\\begin{pmatrix}3\\\\1\\end{pmatrix}$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Lengths double, so the image is not congruent."},{"q":"If $0<k<1$, the image of an enlargement is","options":["smaller than the object","larger than the object","the same size","always upside down"],"correct":0,"explain":"A fractional scale factor gives a reduction."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Rotate $A(-4,4)$, $B(-1,7)$, $C(-1,4)$ through $270^\\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin.","a":"$A'(4,4)$, $B'(7,1)$, $C'(4,1)$"},{"q":"Rotate $(5,-2)$ through $90^\\circ$ clockwise about the origin.","a":"$(-2,-5)$"},{"q":"Rotate $(3,1)$ through $180^\\circ$ about $(1,2)$.","a":"$(2(1)-3,\\ 2(2)-1)=(-1,3)$"},{"q":"Give the order of rotational symmetry of (a) a regular octagon (b) a rhombus (c) the letter H.","a":"(a) 8 (b) 2 (c) 2"},{"q":"Enlarge $P(-2,-1)$, $Q(-1,0)$, $R(0,-1)$ by scale factor 4 from the origin.","a":"$P'(-8,-4)$, $Q'(-4,0)$, $R'(0,-4)$"},{"q":"Enlarge $P(5,-5)$, $Q(10,-5)$, $R(10,5)$ by scale factor $0.4$ from the origin.","a":"$P'(2,-2)$, $Q'(4,-2)$, $R'(4,2)$"},{"q":"The image of a spider seen through a magnifying glass is 4 times its actual length. The image is 6 cm long. Find the spider's actual length.","a":"1.5 cm"},{"q":"A triangle of area 12 cm² is enlarged with scale factor 3. Find the area of the image.","a":"$12\\times3^2=108$ cm²"},{"q":"Enlarge the point $(4,2)$ by scale factor 3 from the centre $(2,1)$.","a":"$(2,1)+3(2,1)=(8,4)$"},{"q":"Rotate $(5,3)$ through $90^\\circ$ anticlockwise about $(2,1)$.","a":"$(3,2)\\to(-2,3)$, then add $(2,1)$: $(0,4)$"}],"theory":[{"q":"$A(2,1)$ maps to $A'(-1,2)$ and $B(4,1)$ maps to $B'(-1,4)$ under a rotation. Find the centre and angle of rotation.","steps":["The centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of $AA'$. Midpoint $(0.5,\\,1.5)$; gradient of $AA'$ $=\\dfrac{2-1}{-1-2}=-\\tfrac13$, so the bisector has gradient 3: $y-1.5=3(x-0.5)$, that is $y=3x$.","For $BB'$: midpoint $(1.5,\\,2.5)$; gradient $\\dfrac{4-1}{-1-4}=-\\tfrac35$, so the bisector has gradient $\\tfrac53$: $y-2.5=\\tfrac53(x-1.5)$, that is $y=\\tfrac53x$.","Solving $3x=\\tfrac53x$ gives $x=0$, $y=0$: the centre is the **origin**.","Angle: $OA$ has gradient $\\tfrac12$ and $OA'$ has gradient $-2$; the product is $-1$, so the angle is $90^\\circ$. $A$ is in the first quadrant and $A'$ in the second, so the turn is **$90^\\circ$ anticlockwise**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Show that an enlargement with scale factor $-1$ from the origin is the same as a rotation of $180^\\circ$ about the origin. Is it a rigid motion?","steps":["Enlargement with $k=-1$: $(x,y)\\to(-1\\cdot x,\\,-1\\cdot y)=(-x,-y)$.","Rotation of $180^\\circ$ about the origin: $(x,y)\\to(-x,-y)$. The rules are identical, so the transformations are the same.","Since $|k|=1$, every length is unchanged, so this particular enlargement **is** a rigid motion: the image is congruent to the object."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A photograph 10 cm wide and 15 cm high is enlarged so that it is 25 cm wide. Find (a) the scale factor (b) the new height (c) how many times larger the area is, and the new area.","steps":["(a) $k=\\dfrac{25}{10}=2.5$.","(b) New height $=2.5\\times15=37.5$ cm.","(c) Area factor $=k^2=6.25$. Original area $=10\\times15=150$ cm², so new area $=6.25\\times150=937.5$ cm². Check: $25\\times37.5=937.5$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A map has scale $1:50\\,000$. (a) Explain why this is an enlargement and give the scale factor from ground to map. (b) Two towns are 7.2 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they? (c) A farm covers 2 cm² on the map. Find its real area in km².","steps":["(a) The map is a similar copy of the ground, every length reduced by the same factor: an enlargement with $k=\\dfrac{1}{50\\,000}$.","(b) Real distance $=7.2\\times50\\,000=360\\,000$ cm $=3.6$ km.","(c) Areas scale by $50\\,000^2=2.5\\times10^9$. Real area $=2\\times2.5\\times10^9=5\\times10^9$ cm². Since $1\\text{ km}^2=10^{10}$ cm², the farm covers **0.5 km²**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Compare translation, reflection, rotation and enlargement. For each, say whether lengths, angles and orientation are kept, and which are rigid motions.","steps":["**Translation:** lengths and angles kept; orientation kept. Rigid.","**Reflection:** lengths and angles kept; orientation **reversed**. Rigid.","**Rotation:** lengths and angles kept; orientation kept (the shape is turned, not flipped). Rigid.","**Enlargement:** angles kept, but lengths multiplied by $|k|$ and areas by $k^2$; orientation kept (a negative $k$ adds a half-turn, which does not flip the shape). **Not** rigid unless $k=\\pm1$: the image is similar, not congruent."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can find the order of rotational symmetry of a shape.","I can rotate points about the origin through $90^\\circ$, $180^\\circ$ and $270^\\circ$.","I can rotate about another centre and find a centre of rotation.","I can enlarge a shape by a positive, fractional or negative scale factor.","I can find the centre and scale factor of an enlargement.","I can use $k$ and $k^2$ for lengths and areas in real
